author: Rahul kp
title: Provision
simple_words: A provision is charged to profit for a known loss or liability. A reserve is profit kept back for the future.

definitions.meaning: Amount charged against profit for a known liability, or fall in asset value, where the amount cannot be fixed exactly and is estimated.
Amount set aside out of profit, after profit is found, to strengthen the business or for a general or specific purpose.

key_points: A ==provision== is a charge, so it is debited to Profit and Loss before profit is found.
A ==reserve== is an appropriation: it is made out of profit already earned.
!!Provision is made even in a year of loss!!; a reserve needs profit.
Free reserves like general reserve can be used for dividend; a provision cannot.

rows: Known liability or asset fall, amount estimated

insight.punchline: Provision cuts profit; reserve uses it!
insight.text: A provision is deducted to arrive at profit, while a reserve is created only from the profit that remains.

memory_trick.explanation: Provision is charged first, so profit comes after it. Reserve is Retained out of profit already earned.

steps: Read what the amount is for
Out of profit kept back? Reserve
Check free or not for dividend
exam_tip: In MCQs, if the item reduces profit before profit is found, choose provision. If it comes after profit, choose reserve.

doubt.question: Is a provision always shown as a liability?
doubt.answer: No. A provision for a liability, like tax, is shown as a liability. A provision for doubtful debts is deducted from debtors.

mistakes.wrong: Provision is an appropriation of profit
mistakes.right: Provision is a charge against profit; a reserve is the appropriation.

mistakes.wrong: No provision is needed in a loss year
mistakes.right: A provision is needed even in a loss year, as it is a charge.

mistakes.wrong: All reserves can be paid out as dividend
mistakes.right: Only free reserves can be distributed; capital reserve and securities premium are not freely distributable.

applicability: Accounting concept; Companies Act dividend rules in outline

Checker 1: Table row 4 (Effect on profit), Reserve cell: 'Profit is already found' does not actually state the effect. It should read: 'Does not reduce net profit; reduces the profit available for distribution (divisible profit).'

Checker 1: Memory trick 'P = Profit after charge' is vague and could be read as 'provision = profit'. A clearer version: 'Provision → P&L A/c (charged before profit); Reserve → Retained out of profit (P&L Appropriation).'
Checker 1: Doubt answer: a short addition would help. Like the provision for doubtful debts, the provision for depreciation is also deducted from the related asset rather than shown as a liability.
